title: Microinjection of Corn Planthopper, Peregrinus maidis, Embryos for CRISPR/Cas9 Genome Editing
protocol: Plant a minimum of four pots of corn per week per rearing cage, with 3-4 seeds per pot.
Grow in an insect-free environment.
Place plants inside a 30 cm x 30 cm x 60 cm cage when they are ~5 weeks old.
Obtain P. maidis adults (~500) from a research laboratory or the wild.
Place obtained adults into an insect-proof cage with 9-12 corn plants (3-4 pots).
Maintain the colony in an insect-rearing incubator at 25 °C, with at least 70% humidity and a 14:10 light cycle.
Remove all initial adults after four days of egg laying to generate an age-calibrated colony.
Allow embryos laid in the cage to hatch and age naturally.
Move 5-week-old P. maidis insects (adults) to fresh corn plants for weekly subculture by collecting with an aspirator.
Release the collected adults into a clean cage with fresh corn plants.
Prepare fresh age-calibrated cages every week to maintain a steady supply of young adults.
Water the pots in the cages twice daily.
Periodically clip stalks and remove decaying plant material from the cages.
Replace with fresh corn pots as needed.
Make egg collection dishes by pouring 1% w/v agarose in water into clean 100 mm x 15 mm Petri dishes.
Store the oviposition medium at 4 °C after it solidifies.
Prepare a 10% w/v sucrose solution.
Store the sucrose solution at -20 °C for up to one month.
Cut a hole in the bottom of a 1 oz cup.
Glue a screen over the hole for air exchange.
Cut plastic paraffin wax film into 5 cm x 5 cm squares.
Collect approximately 15 1-week-old adult females from an age-calibrated P. maidis colony.
Chill the insects briefly on ice before sexing.
Transfer the chilled insects to the adult container.
Seal the cup with one layer of plastic paraffin wax film, stretching it 3-4 times its original size.
Apply 400 µL of 10% w/v sucrose solution to the top of the first seal.
Add a second layer of plastic paraffin wax film, stretching as before.
Place the adult chamber on an egg collection dish with the plastic paraffin wax film side directly on the oviposition medium.
Wrap the entire egg-laying chamber with plastic wrap without covering the air holes.
Incubate each egg-laying chamber at 25 °C with 70% humidity and a 14:10 light cycle.
Change the sandwich of plastic paraffin wax film and 10% w/v sucrose solution daily.
Remove any water that accumulates inside the cup.
Set up a stereomicroscope-based microinjection system in a humidified space or hood (at least 70% humidity).
Check the oviposition medium for eggs after the desired egg-lay period.
Use fine forceps to carefully dig out any eggs laid in the agarose and place them on the surface of the agarose to keep them moist.
Apply a strip of 1 mm x 15 mm double-sided tape on a 22 mm x 30 mm coverslip.
Place the coverslip tape-side up on the oviposition medium.
Pick up each individual egg from the agar surface using a fine brush.
Move picked eggs to the double-sided tape using a fine brush.
Remove any eggs that are completely white or have black coloration.
Place healthy semi-transparent eggs on their side with the larger end stuck on the double-sided tape.
Keep eggs in a high-humidity environment, such as a Petri dish cast with a layer of 1% agar on the bottom.
Pull quartz needles using a Flaming/Brown type micropipette puller.
Bevel the pulled quartz needles using a micropipette beveler.
Secure pulled needles using double-sided sticky tape in a clear container until ready to use.
Prepare injection solution by combining 0.5 µL of Cas9 protein with 0.5 µL of sgRNA and 1 µL of phenol red buffer, making the final volume 5 µL.
Vortex the injection solution briefly.
Centrifuge the prepared injection solution for 3 min at maximum speed.
Backfill the injection needle carefully to leave the injection mix near the tapered end of the needle.
Remove bubbles from the tip of the needle if present.
Carefully place the backfilled needle into the needle holder.
Tighten the stainless steel collar to secure the needle in place during microinjection.
Gently stroke the beveled tip of the needle with a fine, dampened paintbrush.
Deliver bursts of air pressure to the needle using the injection system.
Check if the needle is ready for injection when small amounts of solution can leave the tip.
Prepare a microinjection platform by filling a clean Petri dish with 1% agar.
Place a coverslip containing ~25 embryos on the prepared agar platform.
Perform all injection steps inside a humidified hood (~70% humidity).
Check the injection pressure by placing the needle tip in a drop of water and initiating the injection cycle.
Insert the needle into the larger end of the embryo from the left side.
Deliver the injection solution into the egg.
Pull out the needle quickly after delivering the solution.
Place the coverslip with injected embryos on the surface of a new 1% agar dish.
Transfer the dish to a humidity chamber for incubation and hatching.
Put the hatching chamber in a 25 °C incubator for 6 days.
Transfer surviving embryos to a Petri dish with water-moistened filter paper using clean water and a fine brush.
Seal the Petri dish with plastic paraffin wax film.
Hold the sealed Petri dish at 25 °C to allow the embryos to hatch.
Check the embryos for survival starting 6 days post-injection.
Transfer first instar nymphs, using a fine brush, to a Petri dish containing leaf clippings when they start hatching around day 8.
Seal the dish with plastic paraffin wax film.
Incubate the sealed dish on leaf cuttings at 25 °C for 48 hours.
Transfer all 2-day-old nymphs from a round of injections to a rearing cage with corn plants using a fine brush.
Place hatchlings gently in the whorl of the corn plant.
Rear insects under conditions ensuring proper temperature, humidity, and regular transfers to fresh corn plants.
Screen progeny for expected phenotypes.
Place individuals exhibiting the desired phenotype into their own cage to establish homozygous lines.
